description: Estimate source strength by injecting symmetric charge probes and reading only passive capacitor slew, avoiding explicit comparator bias until after the first viable source wins startup.
mathematical_formalization: strength_i ≈ (ΔV_probe_i / Δt) / Q_injected with comparator bias held at 0 during probe phase.
implementation_hypothesis: A purely charge-domain probe might be cheaper than RC rankers when ramps are extremely slow and source impedance is the main uncertainty.
experiment_seed: Compare probe energy versus startup-time benefit against the time-constant ranker in the 1:5 and 1:20 impedance cases.

closest_prior_art.title: Fully Integrated Startup at 70 mV of Boost Converters for Thermoelectric Energy Harvesting
Single- and multi-source battery-less power management circuits for piezoelectric energy harvesting systems

novelty_claim: This is the lowest-overhead source-awareness path; it survives only if the passive probe remains materially cheaper than explicit arbitration hardware.
differentiation: Avoids helper rails and explicit comparator bias during the earliest startup stage.
predicted_failure_mode: Capacitor mismatch and injected charge loss make the probe estimate too inaccurate to justify the complexity.
